key_insight: A multimodal deep learning model that combines text from presenting complaints with numerical vital signs can improve emergency triage prediction by using self-attention to capture both local and global feature relationships.
clinical_relevance: This approach may support faster, more consistent triage prioritization in emergency departments by helping automate risk assessment from routine electronic health record data.
method: Trained a multimodal architecture on both tabular vital-sign data and complaint text.
Used self-attention to model feature dependencies across modalities.
Compared performance against a baseline triage model.
evidence_signal: The model was developed and validated on 11,102 emergency department triage records from Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia and improved accuracy, F1-score, and ROC AUC versus baseline.
watch_item: Performance gains are promising, but the abstract does not report external validation, so real-world generalizability across hospitals and patient populations remains uncertain.
paper_title: Multimodal Attention-based Deep Learning for Emergency Triage with Electronic Health Records
